result:
Agreed, the what is settled. One choice is still open, and it is about how to build it, not what it does. Pick one and I will write the design straight away.

1. **Add it to the taproom app (recommended).** Batch tracking becomes a new section of the Flask app you already run, in the same SQLite database. You have one thing to run, update and back up on the Pi. The cost is that a fault in batch tracking could stop the taproom tabs too.
2. **Run a separate small app on the same Pi.** It has its own database file, so a fault in one cannot touch the other. The cost is two services to start, update and back up.

I dropped off-the-shelf brewery software. You already have a working app on your own hardware, and a hosted product would not reuse any of it.

I recommend option 1. Batch tracking is a small addition, and one app on one Pi is easier for a small team to keep alive.

This is a project-sized piece of work. I will write the design to `specs/` and a reviewer will read it first. I may come back once with a few questions. The folder is not under version control yet, so I will also run `git init` to commit the design, unless you object.

Option 1 or option 2?
